items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-27
items.q: Louis, uh, Louis Armstrong, he was Hot Five or Hot Seven or something like that. And they used to do a broadcast from there.

ctx.x: I got, well, uh, he, it was, he had about a six or seven piece orchestra. Uh-huh. Louis, uh, Louis Armstrong, he was Hot Five or Hot Seven or something like that. And they used to do a broadcast from there. And he talked, he talked 90% through the show. Yeah. And it was the same thing with Phil Harris when he was at the Blue Room. Uh-huh. They used to talk and talk and talk and talk. I mean, there was very little music that you could hear. Really. And Phil Harris, oh, they loved Phil in New Orleans. They loved…
How big was Suburban Gardens to support these bands and bring them in from out of town?

items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-20
items.q: He followed us in when we left. I knew Louie, and then I knew Louie.

ctx.x: Mmhm. That's your uncle also? Yeah, he was, you see, he lived at the Lambs Club. Mm-hmm. 130 West 44th Street. The same person as Moyes Hirsch? Yeah. Oh, change his name. Just change his name. And this is one of my other uncles. No. That's Mendelov. I saved this up. This is quite a, I've read a book on Louie. Do you remember him when he was here? Louie? Yeah. I've got a picture of Louie Armstrong sitting, standing in front of Suburban Gardens. Mm-hmm. I don't think you ever heard of Suburban Gardens. Oh, yes. We…
You don't get the lavalier microphone. Yeah. I'm going to go get this here now.
